This is f*cking insane. Yann LeCun won the Turing Award for the neural nets behind today's AI, ran AI at Meta for 12 years, then walked out to build his own lab. Now he says the whole agent boom is built on the wrong thing:

"Basing agentic systems on LLMs is a recipe for disaster

How can a system possibly plan a sequence of actions if it can't predict the consequences of its actions?"

In 34 seconds, the man who helped invent deep learning tells everyone shipping agents what is missing underneath them

Predict The World → Predict Your Action → Plan The Steps → Reach The Goal

An LLM guesses the next word. It never checks what its last move did to the world

That is why the agents that work today don't run on the model alone. They run inside a loop that checks every step before the next one

The people who build that loop around the model are the ones whose agents don't fall apart on step 5

See how the harness, the loops and the graph fit around the model in the guide below ↓

This new essay by Steven Pinker is so illuminating that I don’t know where to begin.

Let me start with intelligence.

The whole debate about human-level artificial intelligence assumes that intelligence is some unidimensional universal construct.

But this is not true. Even if IQ captures differences within our species, this does not work across species. A cat can solve in a split second problems that we struggle with.

With machines, it’s even clearer. A boat is more powerful than a human. But it will never climb the stairs.

The problem with treating intelligence as a unidimensional, universal construct is that it generates extreme scenarios:

Once “intelligence” gets high enough, AI will either destroy humanity or solve all its problems.

But this ignores bodies. Infrastructure. Physical limits.

In reality, AI will probably solve some problems and create others.

We should be working together to reduce the harms and increase the benefits, without falling prey of catastrophic scenarios.

And now the most unsettling part.

In some circles is emerging the idea that machines may become conscious and that that we should also protect machines from us.

Suppose you give a chatbot the tiniest moral weight because there’s a chance it might suffer. If you add up those weights, eventually saving enough chatbots could justify killing a person.

The idea of conscious machines is extremely dangerous.

We should build machines that help us our problems, not machines that are conscious and create even more problems.

*

Tarbell does not just shape public perception about AI.

Tarbell's reporting also shapes Congressional briefings.

Tarbell is funded by Coefficient Giving -- funded by Dustin Moskowitz's Good Ventures Foundation -- which sits on top of billions of dollars of Moskowitz's Series A Anthropic stock.

Tarbell has an incentive to help Anthropic.

The bigger Anthropic stock grows, the bigger the money pile underneath GVF grows. And the bigger that money pile grows, the bigger GVF's large nonprofit network can grow -- of which Tarbell is one node.

That means shaping stories of Anthropic's competitors -- like Nvidia -- in the least favorable way possible.

It also means pushing chip export restrictions.

Open source models built on American chips directly threaten Anthropic's business model.

It also means pushing AI doom and pushing for more regulations -- which could give Anthropic a government-regulated monopoly in AI.

A government regulated monopoly is an information ecosystem monopoly.

And that is the goal.

With Tarbell reporting making its way into Congressional briefings, Tarbell is also shaping policy in ways that benefit Anthropic.

Democrats couldn't be happier. Anthropic shares similar left-wing values and is aligned with the Democrats, increasingly even sharing people, including key former Obama administration personnel.

A closed model ecosystem controlled by Anthropic and the Democrats allows them to try to put the genie of AI back in the bottle and try to re-establish control over American tech.

They want to do with AI what they did with search engines like Google and social media networks like Facebook and Twitter.

And it is all playing out before our eyes.
